events.body: Thanks @brunoerg. Forced push efe0dfcf1e5c431c62dc9ac4fd2c2d97a62814fe addressing https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36291#discussion_r4128116862. See [DERSIG cases diff](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/a0ce5b2629394af8e5d5fde6459e27d2c935d43e..a2c90fb8d24189586c734253de44b930f43efac8) and [STRICTENC cases diff](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/a2c90fb8d24189586c734253de44b930f43efac8..efe0dfcf1e5c431c62dc9ac4fd2c2d97a62814fe)

ACK efe0dfcf1e5c431c62dc9ac4fd2c2d97a62814fe

I ran the 11 new rows through btclib's script interpreter and each gives the expected result and error code.

@ViniciusCestarii can you re-write the pull request descriptions of your mutations without having to nest html in it? Maybe just give every mutation as its minimized diff? The pull request description gets added to every merge commit and all the formatting makes it harder to render the same everywhere and a bit harder to read.

comments.body: d34cd78bd5ed887f136e0f09a98b519c71470516: do we really need this 8-byte vector test? As far as I verified, the mutant is killed with the other test here (3-byte one).

It is not necessary for killing the mutant. My reasoning was to add case that directly tests the lower bound. But thinking back no signature under 9 bytes is valid and the 3 byte case is only worth it because it causes UB. I will drop the 8 byte cases and keep the 3 byte one. Thanks for spotting this.
nit: do these new DERSIG test cases really need a real pubkey? I think an empty pubkey would work, e.g. "0 CHECKSIG NOT"

True, it is better to simplify these tests. I noticed this also applies for the sigs on cases of STRICTENC, so I simplified both DERSIG and STRICTENC added tests on efe0dfcf1e5c431c62dc9ac4fd2c2d97a62814fe
